title: Make & host multiplayer games - a vibecoding platform
author: Salt-Risk-5136
selftext:
For the last 10 months I've been vibecoding a site that lets you vibecode multiplayer games. It creates a world, uses blender to make assets, hosts the game for you, and lets anyone in the world play it. It's built specifically for great multiplayer.

Feel free to build and host new games on it! It's still early and I'll be making lots of improvements based on your feedback. It's on [kube.new](http://kube.new/), and you can give your Claude Code or Codex agent the 'share' link to make games for free. Also, help me kickstart the Discord :) [https://discord.gg/4uZsGRtGT](https://discord.gg/4uZsGRtGT)

https://preview.redd.it/qn1kjw1hu4vh1.png?width=1722&format=png&auto=webp&s=92a8e2304592720d37a48b2c0d91a1826d0f0ad5

This is really built from scratch in Rust! It has an efficient multiplayer engine built on QUIC networking, a TypeScript scripting interpreter that runs your game, and it lets you edit with friends or Codex/Claude Code (just give them the invite link).

  
 I used Codex and Claude Code to make all the netcode (QUIC datagrams + bidi streams), visuals (custom WGSL shaders), desktop app, Docker containers for hosting, and backend systems for editing games live with other people. The renderer also compiles to WASM; this was really hard but it means we get the best of both worlds, (1) an in-browser editor, and (2) a native desktop app that feels great and is fast.

Some of the hardest parts:  
\- Manually designing all of the QUIC datagram structs that are sent (and proving the netcode's correctness)  
\- Creating a V8 bridge between React and TypeScript, so that your TS scripts can call functions to affect the game which is running on Rust  
\- Building a React GUI system in a Rust project (involved a custom React interpreter)  
\- Porting the renderer to the browser using WASM  
\- Architecting the editor\_server so you can edit and playtest with friends  
\- I wrote a few devlogs about my favorite parts. [kube.new/blog](http://kube.new/blog)

A lot of this was done before AI was good at 3D and networking. You might consider this to be either be good or bad. I'll take this as a benefit, since it forced me to have a great understanding of all the systems even in the 80k+ LOC codebase (and that's excluding tests!).

Again, [kube.new](http://kube.new/) and [https://discord.gg/4uZsGRtGT](https://discord.gg/4uZsGRtGT) :D

comments.author: LVermeulen
comments.body:
This looks technically impressive, but it seems like a platform like this needs some unique gameplay or focus. There is already a ton of AI vibe coding platforms with Minecraft likes and other simple games - and now these games are easily made without a platform by anyone with the AI tools directly.

Without a unique game experience, why would players come? And if players don't come why would creators

replies.author: Salt-Risk-5136
replies.body: True, marketplaces are hard. We're still looking for novel viral gamemodes, but I think they must exist and simply need to be discovered. I think even with AI tools multiplayer is hard, and we handle it fully for free. Thanks for the feedback!
